exposure: women's socio-demographic characteristics (religion, caste system, wealth quintile, education, media exposure)
outcome: different types of contraceptive methods used (specifically female sterilization)
cohort: The study participants were women from India who participated in the National Family Health Surveys (NFHS/DHS) across four survey periods between 1992-93 and 2015-16.
finding: The study identified that the dominance of female sterilization in India's family planning program is influenced by socio-demographic factors such as religion, caste, wealth, education, parity, and media exposure.
cross-section timing: Data pooled from 1992-93, 1998-99, 2005-06, and 2015-16 NFHS/DHS surveys.
